title: Signal Management
definition: The process of controlling and handling signals in a computer system, including the creation, transmission, and response to signals.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of signals as messages passed between different parts of a computer system. Managing signals ensures that the right message reaches the right place at the right time.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Signal management is a fundamental aspect of computer systems, enabling efficient communication and coordination between processes. This includes handling interrupts, managing asynchronous events, and ensuring that signals are not lost or delayed.
difficulty_levels.expert: Signal management is a rich field with connections to various disciplines. It touches on topics such as real-time systems, distributed systems, and concurrency control. Signal management is not just about handling individual signals, but also about ensuring that the overall system behaves predictably and reliably, even in the presence of complex interactions and multiple sources of signals.
